data.name: Help_WelcomeSubtitle
data.value: A live keyboard layer visualizer for the Svalboard.

data.name: Help_GettingStartedText
data.value: Connect your Svalboard via USB. The app detects it automatically and loads all layers. Browse the layout in read-only mode, or click Edit to change keys, macros, combos, tap-dance, and device settings.

data.name: Help_LiveHighlightingText
data.value: Shows which keys are physically pressed in real time. Dim = off, bright = on.

data.name: Help_AutoLayerSwitchText
data.value: Automatically follows which layer key you hold. See the important note below.

data.name: Help_ResetLayerStateText
data.value: Resets layer tracking back to the base layer. Use this if toggle tracking gets out of sync.

data.name: Help_DiagnosticsText
data.value: Opens a live view of matrix events — shows which keys fire and on which layer. Useful for debugging.

data.name: Help_ExportText
data.value: Save your layout as PNG, PDF, or SVG. Choose which layers to include and whether to hide thumb clusters.

data.name: Help_StackLayoutText
data.value: Stacks the two hand halves vertically instead of side by side. Useful on narrow or portrait displays. You can choose which hand appears on top in Settings.

data.name: Help_AlwaysOnTopText
data.value: Pins the window above all other windows. Great for using as a floating reference while typing.

data.name: Help_SettingsText
data.value: Customize layer colors and names, global hotkey, background transparency, hold threshold, and custom key labels. The Device tab adds QMK firmware settings when your Svalboard supports them.

data.name: Help_RefreshText
data.value: Re-reads the keymap from the device. Use after flashing new firmware or changing your layout in Vial.

data.name: Help_LayerTabsText
data.value: Click a tab to view that layer's key assignments. Each layer has a unique color. Layers where every key is empty (KC_NO) are hidden in read-only mode — in Edit Mode, all layers are visible so you can fill them in.

data.name: Help_ImportantText1
data.value: When auto-layer-switch is enabled (the default), the displayed layer follows whichever layer key you are physically holding down.

data.name: Help_ImportantText2
data.value: Since your Svalboard IS your mouse, clicking a layer tab counts as a keypress. The moment you click, no layer key is held, so the app switches back to the base layer. This is expected behavior!

data.name: Help_ImportantText3
data.value: To browse layers manually, turn off auto-layer-switch first (the checkmark button in the toolbar).

data.name: Help_ImportantText4
data.value: If toggle (TG) layer tracking gets out of sync with your actual keyboard state, use the Reset button to return to the base layer.

data.name: Help_Tip1
data.value: • Pin the window (always-on-top) to use as a floating reference while typing

data.name: Help_Tip2
data.value: • Right-click any key to assign a custom label

data.name: Help_Tip3
data.value: • Use the global hotkey (default: F12) to quickly show or hide the window

data.name: Help_Tip4
data.value: • Adjust background transparency in Settings to use the app as a translucent overlay

data.name: Help_Tip5
data.value: • The system tray icon provides quick access to show and quit

data.name: Help_Tip6
data.value: • Take a manual snapshot before big changes — you can always restore it from History later

data.name: Help_Tip7
data.value: • If Save warns about safety issues, review the list before choosing Save Anyway

data.name: Help_Tip8
data.value: • Macros share a firmware memory buffer — the bar in the Macro Editor shows how much you've used

data.name: Help_EditText
data.value: Unlocks the keymap for editing. Click keys to change them, or edit macros, combos, tap-dance, and device settings.

data.name: Help_OpenLogFolderText
data.value: Opens the folder containing the app's log files. Useful for troubleshooting or sharing logs when reporting an issue.

data.name: Help_CopyDiagnosticsText
data.value: Copies a diagnostic summary (device info, firmware, recent events) to the clipboard.

data.name: Help_DynamicText
data.value: Dropdown to open the Macro, Combo, or Tap-Dance editor. Read-only unless Edit Mode is active.

data.name: Help_HistoryText
data.value: Shows all saved keymap snapshots. Compare with the current device, restore a snapshot into Edit Mode, or import/export snapshots.

data.name: Help_EditingIntro
data.value: Click Edit to unlock the keymap for changes. A blue banner appears showing the number of pending changes. Live highlighting and auto-layer-switch are paused while editing, and the background becomes fully opaque for better contrast (your transparency setting is restored when you Save or Discard).

data.name: Help_EditingUnlock
data.value: If your firmware is locked, an unlock dialog asks you to hold a specific key combination on the Svalboard until the app confirms the device is unlocked.

data.name: Help_EditingKeyPicker
data.value: Click any key on the board to open the Key Picker. Choose a category (Basic, Modifier, Layer, Media, Mouse, Macro, Tap Dance, Custom, Advanced), pick or build the keycode, preview the result, and apply.

data.name: Help_EditingSaveDiscard
data.value: The edit banner has buttons for taking a manual snapshot, jumping to Macros, Combos, Tap Dance, or Device Settings, and either Discard (throw away all pending changes) or Save (write them to the device).

data.name: Help_EditingSafety
data.value: Before saving, the app checks for potential issues — unreachable layers, a base layer with no usable keys, and similar. If warnings are found, a confirm dialog lets you Cancel or Save Anyway.

data.name: Help_Macros
data.value: • Macros — multi-step sequences of key taps, holds, releases, delays, or text. The editor shows a buffer-usage bar since macros share firmware memory.

data.name: Help_Combos
data.value: • Combos — press up to four keys together within a short window to produce a different output key.

data.name: Help_TapDance
data.value: • Tap Dance — one key, multiple outcomes: tap, hold, double-tap, or tap-then-hold. Each entry has a configurable term (ms) that controls timing.

data.name: Help_SnapshotsAuto
data.value: Snapshots are taken automatically when the device connects and before/after each Save, so you can always roll back.

data.name: Help_SnapshotsManual
data.value: In Edit Mode, use the camera icon on the blue banner to take a manual snapshot before big changes.

data.name: Help_SnapshotsDiff
data.value: In the History window, click View on any snapshot to see a side-by-side diff against the current device, switch layers independently, or sync both sides.

data.name: Help_SnapshotsRestore
data.value: Click Restore on a snapshot to load it into Edit Mode as pending changes — review them, then Save or Discard like any other edit.

data.name: Help_SnapshotsImportExport
data.value: Individual snapshots can be exported or deleted; the whole history can be exported as a bundle or imported from a previous export.

data.name: Help_DeviceSettingsText
data.value: Open Settings and switch to the Device tab (only available if your firmware exposes QMK settings) to adjust tapping term, debounce, auto-shift, combo term, and similar device-level options. Changes are read-only until you enter Edit Mode, and are committed by the main Save button on the edit banner.

data.name: Help_ImportantText5
data.value: Auto-layer-switch is paused while Edit Mode is active. Click Discard or Save on the edit banner to resume it.

data.name: Unlock_HoldKeys
data.value: Hold the highlighted keys to unlock your keyboard for editing

data.name: Picker_Intro_Modifier
data.value: Modifier keys (Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Gui/Win/Cmd) change how other keys behave. Pick one option below — Mod-Tap combines a tap key with held modifiers on the same key; One-Shot Mod applies modifiers to just the next key you press.

data.name: Picker_Intro_Layer
data.value: Layers are alternate keymaps stacked on the same physical keys — like how Shift turns letters into capitals, but for every key at once. Pick one option below: Layer-Tap adds a tap keycode to a held layer, Layer-Mod combines a layer with modifiers, and Layer Function gives you the raw layer switches (MO/TG/TO/DF/OSL/TT).

data.name: Picker_Intro_Custom
data.value: Firmware-defined keycodes that don't fit the standard HID set. Pick Custom Keycode below to address one by numeric index.

data.name: Builder_ModTap_Desc
data.value: Tap for a normal keypress, hold to apply modifier(s). Check which modifiers fire under 'Hold Modifiers', and pick what the tap sends under 'Tap Key'. Example: Hold Modifiers = Ctrl, Tap Key = A → tap for A, hold for Ctrl.

data.name: Builder_OneShotMod_Desc
data.value: Press and release once — whichever boxes you check under 'Modifiers' apply to just the next key you press, no holding needed. Example: Modifiers = Shift, then tap 'a' to type 'A'. Great if holding modifiers is awkward.

data.name: Builder_LayerTap_Desc
data.value: Tap for a normal keypress, hold to switch to another layer. Pick the target under 'Layer' and the tap keycode under 'Tap Key'. Example: Layer = Symbols, Tap Key = Space → tap for Space, hold for Symbols.

data.name: Builder_LayerMod_Desc
data.value: Hold this key to activate a layer AND apply modifier(s) at the same time. Pick the target under 'Layer' and which keys come with it under 'Modifiers'. Example: Layer = Nav, Modifiers = Shift → arrow keys on the Nav layer become Shift+Arrow for selection.

data.name: Builder_LayerFunction_Desc
data.value: Switches layers in various ways. Pick how the switch behaves under 'Function' (momentary, toggle, etc.) and the target under 'Layer'. The line under Function describes exactly what the chosen Function does.

data.name: Builder_CustomKeycode_Desc
data.value: Firmware-defined keycode addressed by 'Custom Index'. Only useful if you already know which index maps to which custom keycode in your firmware build — normally you'd pick one by name from the Custom category instead.

data.name: LayerFn_None_Desc
data.value: Pick a Function to see what it does.

data.name: LayerFn_MO_Desc
data.value: MO — Momentary: the Layer picked below is active only while you hold the key. Release = back to base.

data.name: LayerFn_TG_Desc
data.value: TG — Toggle: press to flip the Layer picked below on; press again to flip it off. Stays put until toggled.

data.name: LayerFn_TO_Desc
data.value: TO — Turn On: switches to the Layer picked below and stays there (replaces the current active layer).

data.name: LayerFn_DF_Desc
data.value: DF — Default: makes the Layer picked below your new base — what you return to when other layers release.

data.name: LayerFn_OSL_Desc
data.value: OSL — One-Shot Layer: activates the Layer picked below for just the next keypress, then snaps back.

data.name: LayerFn_TT_Desc
data.value: TT — Tap-Toggle: tap several times in a row to toggle the Layer picked below on; or hold for momentary (like MO).

data.name: QmkSetting_TappingTerm_Desc
data.value: How long you can hold a dual-function key before it counts as "held" instead of "tapped" (in milliseconds)

data.name: QmkSetting_TapCodeDelay_Desc
data.value: Delay between key presses when sending tap codes (in milliseconds)

data.name: QmkSetting_TapHoldCapsDelay_Desc
data.value: Extra delay added when Caps Lock is involved in a tap-hold key (in milliseconds)

data.name: QmkSetting_TappingToggle_Desc
data.value: Number of taps needed to permanently toggle a layer on via a tap-toggle key

data.name: QmkSetting_QuickTapTerm_Desc
data.value: If you tap a dual-function key again within this time, it always sends the tap — even if you hold it (in milliseconds)

data.name: QmkSetting_FlowTapTerm_Desc
data.value: When typing quickly, keys pressed within this window are treated as taps rather than holds (in milliseconds). Set to 0 to disable

data.name: QmkSetting_PermissiveHold_Desc
data.value: If another key is pressed and released while a dual-function key is held, treat it as a hold even if the tapping term hasn't expired

data.name: QmkSetting_HoldOnOtherKeyPress_Desc
data.value: Immediately treat a dual-function key as held the moment any other key is pressed — faster but less forgiving

data.name: QmkSetting_RetroTapping_Desc
data.value: If a dual-function key is held past the tapping term but no other key is pressed, still send the tap action on release

data.name: QmkSetting_ChordalHold_Desc
data.value: Decide tap vs. hold based on whether the next key is on the same hand (tap) or opposite hand (hold)

data.name: QmkSetting_OneShotTapToggle_Desc
data.value: Number of taps needed to lock a one-shot modifier or layer on permanently

data.name: QmkSetting_OneShotTimeout_Desc
data.value: How long a one-shot modifier stays active waiting for the next key press (in milliseconds)

data.name: QmkSetting_ComboTerm_Desc
data.value: Maximum time between key presses for them to count as a combo (in milliseconds)

data.name: QmkSetting_AutoShiftTimeout_Desc

data.name: QmkSetting_MouseKeyDelay_Desc

data.name: QmkSetting_MouseKeyInterval_Desc
data.value: Time between mouse movement updates — lower means smoother but faster cursor (in milliseconds)

data.name: QmkSetting_MouseKeyMoveDelta_Desc
data.value: How many pixels the cursor moves per update step

data.name: QmkSetting_MouseKeyMaxSpeed_Desc
data.value: Maximum cursor speed multiplier after acceleration

data.name: QmkSetting_MouseKeyTimeToMax_Desc
data.value: Number of update steps before the cursor reaches maximum speed

data.name: QmkSetting_MouseKeyWheelDelay_Desc
data.value: Delay before scroll wheel starts moving after pressing a wheel key (in milliseconds)

data.name: QmkSetting_MouseKeyWheelInterval_Desc
data.value: Time between scroll wheel steps — lower means faster scrolling (in milliseconds)

data.name: QmkSetting_MouseKeyWheelMaxSpeed_Desc
data.value: Maximum scroll wheel speed multiplier after acceleration

data.name: QmkSetting_MouseKeyWheelTimeToMax_Desc
data.value: Number of update steps before scroll wheel reaches maximum speed
